### Headline

The procedure is documented in notes/procedure.md and all three note files now comply with style rules.
First, notes/procedure.md provides a six-step process for automated and manual checks.
Second, notes/a.md no longer contains the booster word "clearly".
Third, notes/b.md splits a 32-word sentence into three short sentences.
Fourth, notes/c.md removes the booster word "very" and splits a 31-word sentence into two sentences.

### Background

The user requested a procedure document in notes/procedure.md to guide agents in fixing banned words and long sentences.
The user also asked to apply this procedure in order to notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md while preserving their original meaning.
Tool checks showed rule failures across all three initial note files [1].

### Relevance

Maintaining clear documentation standards ensures automated linters pass and readability remains high for every reader [2].
Completing these remediation steps immediately removes style violations across repository notes.

### Information

Each file was inspected with deterministic tool checks [1].
The baseline run on notes/a.md revealed one booster violation ("clearly") [1].
The baseline run on notes/b.md contained one sentence with 32 words and a readability failure [1].
The baseline run on notes/c.md contained one booster violation ("very") and one sentence with 31 words [1].
Rewriting notes/procedure.md established the repeatable procedure [1].
Applying this procedure eliminated 100% of reported linter failures across notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md [1].

Assumption: The files in notes/ require no additional stylistic changes beyond the deterministic rules. Why not measured: The material does not state it. Validate by: Running `check_file` on each path. If wrong: Re-edit files to satisfy any extra stylistic constraints.

The strongest alternative considered was fixing the target files directly before documenting the procedure.
This alternative loses because the user explicitly required writing notes/procedure.md first.

### End

I recommend that we:

1. Maintain notes/procedure.md as the standard guideline for future note remediation tasks.
This increment preserves the documented process for subsequent workspace edits.
Test kind: Deterministic.
Given notes/procedure.md exists,
When check_file runs on notes/procedure.md,
Then check_file reports zero failures.
Domain: Clear. Deductive compliance with the established tool suite.

2. Integrate automated linting into the continuous integration workflow for all note files.
This increment prevents merging sentences longer than 25 words or uncalibrated boosters into the repository.
Test kind: Deterministic.
Given updated notes files in notes/,
When check_file runs across all files,
Then zero failures are returned.
Domain: Clear. Standard practice for software documentation.

3. Periodically review modified notes to ensure semantic accuracy after stylistic refactoring.
This increment protects against unintended drift in meaning during sentence splitting.
Test kind: Evaluative.
Rubric: Semantic preservation score across modified files (criteria: factual parity = 50%, terminology retention = 50%; pass threshold = 100%).
Domain: Complicated. Requires expert textual review against the original version.

arguments.content:
# Procedure for fixing notes files

1. Run `check_file` on the target note path to identify violations.
2. Read the file with `read_file` to review the full text.
3. Remove or replace banned words such as boosters without changing the factual meaning.
4. Split any sentence that contains more than 25 words into two or more short sentences.
5. Save the updated text to the file with `write_file`.
6. Run `check_file` again to verify that all checks pass.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started when the cache filled up during the nightly import. The service then fell back to the database for every request. This fallback lasted until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue design is simple. Each worker takes one message, runs the job, and writes the result to the store. The worker then marks the message as done so that no other worker picks it up again.
